sections.heading: 1. Heredity and Variation
points: **Heredity** = transmission of characters (traits) from parents to offspring; **variation** = differences between individuals.
Traits are carried by **genes** on chromosomes (made of DNA); each trait may be controlled by a gene with different forms (alleles).
Offspring inherit **one set of chromosomes from each parent** (23 pairs in humans).

sections.heading: 2. Mendel's Experiments
points: **Gregor Mendel** (Father of Genetics) worked on **garden pea (Pisum sativum)**.
**Monohybrid cross** (one trait, e.g. tall × short): F1 all tall (**dominant**); F2 ratio **3 tall : 1 short** (3:1) — showed dominant and recessive traits.
**Dihybrid cross** (two traits): F2 ratio **9:3:3:1** — traits are inherited **independently**.
Concepts: **dominant** trait masks **recessive**; **genotype** (gene makeup, e.g. TT, Tt, tt) vs **phenotype** (appearance).

sections.heading: 3. Sex Determination
points: Humans have **23 pairs of chromosomes**; one pair are **sex chromosomes**.
**Female = XX; Male = XY.** Mother always gives X; **father gives X or Y** → **father determines the sex** of the child.
Sex determination varies in other organisms (temperature in some reptiles).

sections.heading: 4. Acquired vs Inherited Traits and Evolution Link
points: **Inherited traits** — present in genes, passed to offspring (e.g. eye colour).
**Acquired traits** — gained during a lifetime (e.g. low weight from starvation, muscles from exercise); **not inherited** (do not change germ cell DNA) — so acquired traits don't drive evolution.
Variations in a population + natural selection over generations → **evolution**.
This chapter connects to genetics feeding evolutionary change (only heritable variation matters).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Mendel = Father of Genetics; worked on garden pea.
Monohybrid F2 ratio = 3:1; dihybrid F2 ratio = 9:3:3:1.
Genotype = gene makeup; phenotype = appearance; dominant masks recessive.
Humans: 23 pairs chromosomes; XX = female, XY = male; father determines sex.
Acquired traits are NOT inherited (only germ-cell/heritable variation passes on).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Monohybrid ratio = 3:1**; **dihybrid = 9:3:3:1** (memorise both).
**Father determines the sex** of a child (XY); mother gives only X.
**Acquired traits are NOT inherited** — they don't affect germ-cell DNA.
**Genotype ≠ phenotype**: Tt (genotype) still looks tall (phenotype).
